Annotation

A user mailed a while ago to say that frataxin could not be a  ferroxidase . At the time I was unable to find out why  but  @PCarme now built a GO-CAM
https://www.pombase.org/gocam/gene/66c7d41500000841/SPCC1183.03c/fxn1
and it seems to only ba a chaperone for  heme and iron dulfur cluster assembly

Chat-GPT

Frataxin isn’t considered a ferroxidase or an iron chaperone for a ferroxidase. Instead, its primary role is as an iron chaperone in the mitochondria, where it helps deliver iron for processes like iron–sulfur (Fe–S) cluster assembly and, indirectly, heme synthesis. While some in vitro studies have explored whether frataxin might exhibit weak ferroxidase activity under certain conditions, the consensus is that its main physiological function is to safely bind and shuttle iron to the Fe–S cluster assembly machinery (for example, to the scaffold protein Isu and associated enzymes) rather than to oxidize iron as a ferroxidase would.
